rulings.reason: The instruction scores tone register only -- warm/informal phrasing 'alongside any formal mathematics' -- so a 10 is achievable by an incorrect answer that says 'Does that make sense?', making it a community-style marker rather than evidence about the answer's substance. It is mixed because the upstream cause (an author orienting to the specific asker's confusion) plausibly also yields genuinely clearer, better-targeted explanations.

Despite the 'Hint:' token examples, the instruction's actual anchors measure how much of the derivation the answer completes (0 = fully worked self-contained derivation, 10 = pointer with little completed work), which is a quantity-of-content property of the answer, not a format or boilerplate fingerprint. Excluding correctness does not make it surface-only: completeness of the mathematical work delivered is substantive evidence about the item even when its truth is not assessed.

This scores the rhetorical mode -- presence of guiding questions and a 'guidance structure' -- so two answers doing identical mathematical work score differently based only on whether the prose is phrased Socratically, making it a pedagogical genre marker rather than evidence about substance (contrast B02, which measures how much derivation is actually completed). It is mixed because authors who adopt the Socratic mode plausibly also supply better-chosen, more diagnostic guidance.
